**LangGraph – A Quick Overview**

LangGraph is an open‑source, low‑level orchestration framework created by the LangChain team. It lets developers design, build, and deploy long‑running, stateful AI agents that can perform complex, multi‑step tasks while keeping full control over the workflow.

| Feature | What it means | Source |
|---------|---------------|--------|
| **Graph‑based workflow** | Agents are represented as nodes in a directed graph; edges define the flow of data and control between steps. This structure makes it easier to visualise, debug, and modify agent logic. | [GeeksforGeeks article](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/what-is-langgraph/) |
| **Stateful, long‑running agents** | Unlike short‑lived request‑response bots, LangGraph agents maintain internal state across interactions, enabling tasks that require memory, context, or multi‑turn conversations. | [GitHub repo description](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph) |
| **Low‑level infrastructure** | It is a building block that can be used on its own or as the core engine behind higher‑level LangChain products (e.g., `create_agent`). | [GitHub repo description] |
| **Integration with LangSmith** | Together with LangSmith, LangGraph offers visual debugging, monitoring, and scaling capabilities for production workloads. | [LangChain website](https://www.langchain.com/langgraph) |
| **Flexibility** | You can combine custom Python code, tool calls, and LLM prompts inside the graph, giving fine‑grained control over when and how the LLM is invoked. | [DeepLearning.AI course overview] |
| **Use cases** | Conversational agents, complex task automation, RAG pipelines, multi‑agent coordination, and any scenario that benefits from a declarative, graph‑driven design. | [YouTube tutorial by Tech With Tim] |

In short, LangGraph provides the plumbing for building sophisticated, production‑ready AI agents that need to remember context, orchestrate multiple sub‑tasks, and expose a visual workflow for developers to tweak and debug.
